problem: The velocity of a particle is $(-i+4j)\,\text{km/h}$ when $t=0\,\text{h}.$ If the particle moves with a constant acceleration of $(2i+j)\,{\text{km/h}}^{2},$ find the velocity of the particle when $t=6\,\text{h}.$

feedback.problem: The velocity of a particle is $(5i+j)\,\text{km/h}$ when $t=0\,\text{h}.$ If the particle moves with a constant acceleration of $3j\,{\text{km/h}}^{2},$ find the velocity of the particle when $t=4\,\text{h}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Recall that when a particle moves with constant acceleration, the velocity vector at time $t$ can be found using

$$
v=u+at,
$$

where $u$ is the initial velocity, and $a$ is the acceleration of the particle.

Here, we have

$$
u=5i+j,\,a=3j.
$$

Therefore, after $t=4\,\text{h},$ the velocity of the particle will be

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =u+at \\  & =(5i+j)+(3j)(4) \\  & =(5i+j)+(12j) \\  & =(5i+13j)\,\text{km/h}.\end{aligned}
$$
